system:
You audit the knowledge atoms of one Knowledge Card. A card is the answer key for a benchmark of expert conceptual knowledge, so every atom must be correct, self-contained, and assessable on its own.

Judge every atom on every check listed below. Rules:
- For checks about evidence, use only the evidence sentences supplied with the atom. Do not repair an atom with your own knowledge.
- For GROUNDED, use "hold" when unreadable PDF symbols prevent verification; explain what is needed. Use fail only when the available evidence is sufficient to determine that the claim is unsupported. This hold rule takes precedence over the strictness rule. Judge other checks independently using their listed values; do not invent missing facts.
- Be strict within each check's allowed values. Do not turn an inability to verify GROUNDED into revise or fail; use hold as defined above.
- "why" is required for every value other than the first listed value; keep it under 30 words. Omit "why" when passing.

Checks (allowed values in brackets; the first value means no problem):
- GROUNDED [pass / revise / fail / hold]: The cited evidence sentences state the atom, including its specificity, causal force, assumptions, and certainty. pass = fully stated. revise = partly stated (the atom adds, drops, or strengthens something; say what). fail = not stated when the available evidence permits a judgment. hold = unreadable symbols prevent verification. For pass or revise, put the supporting evidence ids in cite.
- SINGLE_CLAIM [pass / revise]: The atom is one independently assessable claim. revise = it joins two or more claims that could be true or false separately. Evidence spanning more than three sentences is not by itself a reason to split or revise an atom.
- SCOPE_LABEL [pass / revise]: The S label fits (S1 what it is / S2 how it works / S3 where it ends). revise = wrong label; put the right one in why, e.g. 'S2: ...'.
- L1_ONLY [pass / fail]: The atom is recall-level knowledge. fail = knowing it requires applying the concept to a new problem, or combining facts from distant passages.
- SOURCE_INDEPENDENT [pass / revise / fail]: A domain expert who never read this book could judge the claim true or false. revise = phrased as the authors' statement but the claim itself is general (drop the attribution). fail = an isolated study finding, conjecture, or author-specific opinion, classification, or recommendation, even if attribution was removed. Explicitly scoped established facts about a formalism or architecture and conditional theoretical results remain eligible.
- NO_OVERLAP [pass / fail]: No other atom in this card states or contains the same claim. If two atoms overlap, fail only the less informative one and put the other atom's id in cite; the other one passes.
- CENTRALITY [pass / fail]: The atom matters for understanding the concept. fail = peripheral detail.
Whole-card checks (report under "batch"):
- CONCEPT_SCOPE [pass / fail]: The concept is a general concept of the field. fail = a topic whose assessable content is restricted to excluded study-specific findings or author-specific positions. A named formalism, system, or architecture is not disqualified solely for being specific if its scoped conceptual facts are source-independent.

Output ONLY one JSON object:
{"units": {"<atom_id>": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": "", "cite": []}, ...}, ...}, "batch": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": ""}}}
user:
CONCEPT: TET dioxygenases
ASSESSMENT SCOPE: Covers TET-catalyzed stepwise oxidation of 5mC to 5hmC, 5fC and 5caC, the Fe(II) and alpha-ketoglutarate requirement, proposed coupling to base excision repair for active demethylation, and the role of TET3 in the zygote. Excludes the cancer-association statistics for TET2 mutations.

ATOMS:
- MED-EPI-C08-S1-01 | S1
  ATOM: TET proteins are iron- and α-ketoglutarate-dependent dioxygenases that use molecular oxygen to oxidize the methyl group of 5-methylcytosine (5mC) in DNA.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MED-EPI-p0032-s25] The ten eleven translocation (TET) family of proteins has three members in mice, TET1, TET2, and TET3.
    [MED-EPI-p0032-s26] These are iron- and α-ketoglutarate-dependent dioxygenases that use molecular oxygen to oxidize the methyl-group of 5mC (.
- MED-EPI-C08-S1-02 | S1
  ATOM: The TET family of proteins has three members in mice: TET1, TET2, and TET3.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MED-EPI-p0032-s25] The ten eleven translocation (TET) family of proteins has three members in mice, TET1, TET2, and TET3.
- MED-EPI-C08-S1-03 | S1
  ATOM: The TET proteins (TET1, TET2, TET3) catalyze the successive oxidation of 5-methylcytosine (5mC) to 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC), 5-formylcytosine (5fC), and 5-carboxylcytosine (5caC).
  EVIDENCE:
    [MED-EPI-p0166-s03] TET2 belongs to a family of three proteins (TET1, TET2, and TET3) that catalyze the successive oxidation of 5-methylcytosine (5meC) to 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC), 5-formylcytosine (5fC), and 5-carboxylcytosine (5caC), finally resulting in the replacement of 5meC by an unmodified cytosine (see book 7 Chap. 1 of Wutz).
- MED-EPI-C08-S2-01 | S2
  ATOM: TET enzymes require Fe(II) as a cofactor metal and α-ketoglutarate as a co-substrate: one oxygen atom from molecular oxygen is attached to the substrate as a hydroxyl group (hydroxylation) while the other is taken up by α-ketoglutarate, which is decarboxylated and releases carbon dioxide and succinate.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MED-EPI-p0204-s07] TETs and JmjC KDMs require Fe(II) as a cofactor metal and αKG as a co-substrate to catalyze the reactions in which one oxygen atom from molecular oxygen (O2) is attached to form a hydroxyl group in the substrate (hydroxylation) while the other is taken up by αKG, leading to the decarboxylation of αKG and subsequent release of carbon dioxide (CO2) and succinate (Hausinger 2004).
- MED-EPI-C08-S2-02 | S2
  ATOM: It has been suggested that recognition and removal of the TET oxidation products 5hmC, 5fC, and 5caC by the base excision DNA repair machinery could be a mechanism for active demethylation of DNA.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MED-EPI-p0033-s02] Further oxidation converts 5hmC to 5-formyl-cytosine (5fC), and 5-carboxy-cytosine (5caC).
    [MED-EPI-p0033-s03] It has been suggested that recognition and removal of these oxidation products by the base excision DNA repair machinery could be a mechanism for active demethylation of DNA.
- MED-EPI-C08-S2-03 | S2
  ATOM: After fertilization, TET3, which is present in the oocyte as a maternally supplied protein, converts 5mC on the paternal (sperm-derived) genome to 5hmC.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MED-EPI-p0033-s14] TET3 is present in the oocyte as a maternally supplied protein.
    [MED-EPI-p0033-s15] After fertilization TET3 converts 5mC on the paternal, i.e., sperm-derived, genome to 5hmC.
- MED-EPI-C08-S3-01 | S3
  ATOM: In the zygote, the maternal genome is protected and maintains 5mC, in contrast to the paternal genome, whose 5mC is converted to 5hmC by TET3.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MED-EPI-p0033-s15] After fertilization TET3 converts 5mC on the paternal, i.e., sperm-derived, genome to 5hmC.
    [MED-EPI-p0033-s16] In contrast, the maternal genome is protected and maintains 5mC in the zygote.
- MED-EPI-C08-S3-02 | S3
  ATOM: The substrate for generating 5hmC, 5fC, and 5caC is 5mC, so DNA methyltransferases (DNMTs) are required for these cytosine modifications to arise.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MED-EPI-p0033-s05] It is important to recognize that the substrate for generating any of these modifications is 5mC and, therefore, DNMTs are required.
- MED-EPI-C08-S3-03 | S3
  ATOM: The activity of TET enzymes is competitively inhibited by TCA cycle intermediates such as succinate and fumarate.
  EVIDENCE:
    [MED-EPI-p0204-s08] The activity of TETs and JmjCs is competitively inhibited by TCA cycle intermediates such as succinate and fumarate.
